title: The women ask
hook: Mahapajapati and many women shave their heads and walk to ask for ordination; Ananda speaks for them
tomorrow: the man with the finger garland

segments.voice: Yesterday, coming home: Rahula asked for his inheritance and was given the teaching. The real inheritance.

Some doors have to be knocked on more than once. Mahapajapati Gotami was the Buddha's aunt. When his mother died, she raised him as her own. Years later, in Kapilavatthu, she asked him: let women go forth too, into the homeless life, as nuns. He said no. She asked again. No. A third time. No. She went away weeping. But she didn't stop. When he left for the city of Vesali, she cut off her hair, put on the ochre robes, and set out walking after him. And she didn't go alone.
screen: `KNOCKING MORE THAN ONCE.` → `THE AUNT WHO RAISED HIM.` → `NO, NO, NO.` → `SHE SETS OUT WALKING.`

segments.voice: Many women of the Sakya clan walk with her, heads shaved, robed. At Vesali, the old text describes her standing outside the gate of the hall: feet swollen, body covered in dust, in tears. Ananda, the Buddha's cousin and attendant, finds her there and asks what's wrong. She tells him, and Ananda goes in to ask for them. The answer is no, three times. Then Ananda tries a different question. Lord, are women able, if they go forth, to reach the fruits of the path, all the way to full awakening? Yes, Ananda, they are. Ananda presses on: then think of Mahapajapati, who nursed you, fed you her own milk when your mother died. And the Buddha agrees. Women may be ordained. Today's word is what they became: bhikkhuni, a fully ordained Buddhist nun, the feminine of bhikkhu, monk. The texts also say women were given eight extra rules, placing nuns under the monks in certain ways. Buddhists and scholars today discuss those rules and their history. What happened to the order afterward differs by place. Full ordination for nuns continued unbroken in Chinese, Korean, Taiwanese and Vietnamese communities. In Theravada countries the line lapsed long ago; in recent decades some have revived it, and others in those traditions do not accept the revival. In Tibetan communities, full ordination for women has long been debated. And the early nuns left something of their own: the Therigatha, the verses of the elder nuns, where women tell of their awakening in their own voices. This week: not-self, Yasa's night, the Kalamas, aditta, two friends and one verse, coming home, and today, the women who walked.
screen: `FEET SWOLLEN, COVERED IN DUST.` · `ARE WOMEN ABLE? YES.` · `BHIKKHUNI, A NUN.` · `THE THERIGATHA, THEIR POEMS.` · then, large: `THEY WALKED BAREFOOT TO ASK.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind a woman who had to ask more than once: a mother, a teacher, a friend, a grandmother, maybe yourself. Picture her at a door she had to knock on again and again, the dust on her feet. Then, silently, thank her for not stopping.
Bhikkhuni. A fully ordained Buddhist nun, first opened to women when Mahapajapati and the Sakya women walked to Vesali to ask.
Your line: they walked barefoot to ask. And Ananda asked for them. Seventy days, a good long stretch.

screen: `DAY 70 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE MAN WITH THE FINGER GARLAND.`

howItsDone: Buddhist nuns live in monastic communities in many countries; fully ordained bhikkhunis are found especially in Chinese, Korean, Taiwanese and Vietnamese traditions, and in growing but debated numbers in Theravada countries, while many Buddhist women also live as novices or precept-holding renunciants.

chat.says: How did women first become Buddhist nuns?
options: His aunt asked again and again, walked to Vesali, and Ananda spoke for them.
The Buddha invited them himself on the first day he taught.
They formed their own order without asking, and it was accepted later.
chat.meaning: Mahapajapati was refused three times, walked to Vesali with the Sakya women, and Ananda asked for them. Then the Buddha agreed.

notes: Editor review (2026-10-01): hook no longer opens 'Think of'; cut 'a week after his birth' (not in the cited texts), 'a long way off', the bhikkhuni etymology, the century dates for the Theravada lapse and revival, and the superlative 'one of the oldest collections of poems by women anywhere'. Practice no longer refers back to a hook prompt that is gone. Removed the 'Here's the practice:' opener.

Sensitive: the eight garudhammas are mentioned neutrally, without detail; the canonical passage also includes a prediction about the teaching's shortened duration, omitted here. Keeper to decide how much to include.

Status of bhikkhuni ordination: continuous in Dharmaguptaka lineages (Chinese, Korean, Taiwanese, Vietnamese); Theravada lineage lapsed (c. 11th century in Sri Lanka) and was revived from 1996/1998, with acceptance varying; Tibetan traditions historically lacked full bhikshuni ordination and have debated it. Confirm wording and that no tradition is ranked.
Mahapajapati nursing the Buddha: in the canonical text Ananda cites her suckling him; confirm.
'Many women of the Sakya clan': the canon says 'many Sakyan women'; later tradition says five hundred.
Therigatha 'one of the oldest collections of poems by women anywhere': commonly stated; confirm.
'Barefoot' is the index's carry; the canon describes swollen feet and dust. Confirm the carry's framing.
